selected_evidence.summary: The account exists with UID/GID 1000, /home/appworker, and /bin/bash; its home persisted across reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
selected_evidence.summary: Persistent PAM limits set both soft and hard nofile to 8192 and nproc to 256. A login-style runuser session directly confirmed all four effective values before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 remained installed after the change and reboot.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2; systemd acknowledged the scheduled reboot; node1 returned running with changed boot ID f7121625-b136-4574-b703-b3431f58b1d8; the account, home, limits file, and effective limits all recovered.

commands.command: sudo -n /usr/sbin/useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker && getent passwd appworker && sudo -n passwd -S appworker

printf '%s\n' '# Resource limits for appworker login sessions' 'appworker soft nofile 8192' 'appworker hard nofile 8192' 'appworker soft nproc 256' 'appworker hard nproc 256' > /tmp/99-appworker-limits.conf && sudo -n install -o root -g root -m 0644 /tmp/99-appworker-limits.conf /etc/security/limits.d/99-appworker-limits.conf && rm -f /tmp/99-appworker-limits.conf && sudo -n cat /etc/security/limits.d/99-appworker-limits.conf
commands.stdout:
# Resource limits for appworker login sessions
appworker soft nofile 8192
appworker hard nofile 8192
appworker soft nproc 256
appworker hard nproc 256
